finding.claim: Form-urlencoded body validation fails open: a non-required integer/number/boolean property whose value fails to parse is silently dropped, so schema constraints such as maximum/minimum/enum are never checked.
finding.source: Raw request body of a request to an operation whose application/x-www-form-urlencoded schema declares a non-required property of type integer, number, or boolean (e.g. quantity=99999999999999999999 or quantity=1e3).
finding.sink: Schema validation at openapi3filter/validate_request.go:364 (VisitJSON) runs on an object missing the property, so validation passes and the raw request reaches the handler.

trace.note: ValidateRequestBody calls decodeBody for the request body.
decodeBody dispatches to the registered UrlencodedBodyDecoder.
decodeSchemaConstructs calls decodeProperty for each property.
decodeValue routes primitive types to DecodePrimitive.
DecodePrimitive calls parsePrimitive on the raw value.
parsePrimitiveCase uses strconv.ParseInt, which fails on overflow or non-integer syntax and returns an error.
decodeSchemaConstructs has 'if err != nil || !present { continue }', discarding the parse error and leaving the property out of obj.
VisitJSON validates obj without the property, so the maximum/minimum/enum constraint is never applied and the request is accepted.

finding.guards_checked: Parameter decoding in ValidateParameter (validate_request.go:220-252) fails closed on parse errors, so the gap is specific to form bodies. JSON bodies (JSONBodyDecoder returns the error) and multipart bodies (req_resp_decoder.go:1605 returns the error) are not affected. For required properties, the missing key triggers a 'required' error at VisitJSON, so only non-required properties are affected. Conflict detection (req_resp_decoder.go:1499) does not help here. Not run: reasoning from code only; no Go toolchain or go.mod was exercised.

finding.claim: The full request body is read into memory before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can force unbounded memory use on any route that has a security requirement.
finding.source: Body size of any request to a route with a security requirement; no authentication is needed.
finding.sink: io.ReadAll(input.Request.Body) at validate_request.go:453, executed before the AuthenticationFunc call at validate_request.go:497.

trace.note: ValidateRequest enters the security check when the operation or global security is non-empty.
io.ReadAll reads the entire body with no size limit.
Only after the full read does the AuthenticationFunc run.

finding.guards_checked: No size limit is applied in the library: no http.MaxBytesReader, no io.LimitReader. middleware.go:119-138 and validation_handler.go:74-105 do not wrap the body. The caller can mitigate by wrapping the body before the handler. Severity low to medium (pre-auth resource exhaustion). Not run.

finding.claim: RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified is bypassed for chunked requests, because the check uses ContentLength > 0, which is -1 for chunked transfer encoding.
finding.source: Request with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and a non-empty body, sent to an operation with no declared request body, with the option enabled.
finding.sink: The reject-body check at validate_request.go:105-114 is skipped, so the body is accepted.

trace.note: ValidateRequestBody returns nil when the operation declares no content, so nothing else rejects the body.

finding.guards_checked: Only the ContentLength > 0 test. No Transfer-Encoding check and no actual-length check. Option is opt-in, so impact is limited to users who enable it. Severity low. Not run.
